{
  "ideas": [
    {
      "name": "Local Edge Consistency Voting",
      "levels": ["cell", "tissue"],
      "mechanism": "Each projection is split into 2×2 character cells. For every cell Jev is asked a series of noul questions like \"Is the dominant edge direction north-east?\" for the eight compass directions. The returned probabilities are used to vote on the most likely direction and replace the glyph accordingly. After voting all cells, the revised projection is scored by the VLM. This replaces a monolithic VLM edge re‑render with millions of cheap local judgments.",
      "jev_role": "multiple noul queries per cell (8 direction checks) – typed probability yes/no",
      "hypothesis": "If consistency voting improves coherence, the VLM fidelity score will rise from the baseline 0.34 to >0.40 on at least 80 % of test frames.",
      "cost": "≈40 000 Jev noul calls (100 frames × 50 cells × 8 directions) + 100 VLM evaluations; < $0.10 total.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Learns via distributed, discrete judgments instead of gradient‑based weight updates."
    },
    {
      "name": "Motion Arrow Conflict Resolution",
      "levels": ["tissue", "organ"],
      "mechanism": "For each motion‑arrow glyph the system extracts its direction and the adjacent edge glyphs from the previous frame. Jev receives a single choice question: \"Pick the most plausible motion label among {stay, north, east, south, west, unknown}.\" The choice probabilities are used to suppress arrows with <0.6 confidence and to rewrite them with the top‑voted direction. The corrected projection is then evaluated by the VLM.",
      "jev_role": "choice per arrow – typed selection among named motion labels with probabilities",
      "hypothesis": "After conflict resolution motion recall will increase from 0.27 to ≥0.35 while overall fidelity remains ≥0.32.",
      "cost": "≈20 000 Jev choice calls (100 frames × ~200 arrows) + 100 VLM checks; <$0.08 total.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Uses cheap symbolic arbitration to fix temporal inconsistencies rather than end‑to‑end training."
    },
    {
      "name": "Hierarchical Scoring and Targeted Deliberation",
      "levels": ["organ", "organism"],
      "mechanism": "The VLM first produces an object list for each frame (ground‑truth available). For every detected object Jev is asked a score question: \"On a 0‑5 rubric, how accurately does the projected text describe this object?\" Objects scoring ≤2 are sent to a full VLM reconstruction (expensive), while higher‑scoring objects are left untouched. The final composite fidelity is measured against the baseline where every object receives VLM treatment.",
      "jev_role": "score per object – typed expected value on a 0‑5 accuracy rubric",
      "hypothesis": "The hybrid pipeline will achieve overall fidelity ≥0.88 (vs 0.92 full VLM) while reducing VLM calls by at least 70 %.",
      "cost": "≈10 000 Jev score calls (100 frames × 10 objects) + ~30 VLM calls (30 % of baseline); ≈ $0.15 total.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Implements a selective, hierarchical deliberation schedule rather than uniform back‑propagation."
    },
    {
      "name": "Community Config Evolution via Quantum Seeding",
      "levels": ["family", "community"],
      "mechanism": "Fifty random projector configurations are generated. Each config yields a projection which is handed to Jev with a noul question: \"Is the projected fidelity (estimated by a cheap edge‑density heuristic) above 0.30?\" Configs receiving a yes are kept; quantum‑generated random bytes decide which kept configs are parents for the next generation, and their parameters are recombined (crossover) to form a new population. After five generations the best config is finally evaluated by the VLM. No VLM is used during evolution.",
      "jev_role": "noul per config – typed binary predicate on surrogate fidelity",
      "hypothesis": "After five generations the top evolved config will reach VLM fidelity ≥0.38, surpassing the hand‑tuned baseline of 0.34, without any intermediate VLM calls.",
      "cost": "≈250 Jev noul calls (50 configs × 5 generations) + negligible MothQuantum bytes + 1 final VLM evaluation; <$0.02 total.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Performs an evolutionary search driven by discrete typed judgments, not gradient descent."
    }
  ]
}

request.content:
We have a working research harness that turns a camera feed (short frame sequences) into plain text ("projections": character art with edge glyphs, braille, motion arrows). A vision-language model reconstructs the scene (objects, positions, motion) from the text alone; agreement with ground truth is the projection's fidelity. We measured: brightness-only text 0.18, edge glyphs following edges 0.34, motion arrows over edges 0.33 with motion recall 0.27, a VLM reading the real frames 0.92. Search over projector configs is noise-limited; averaging three VLM critics and promoting on held-out feeds fixed overfitting.

Tools available right now, all via API:
- TypeSafe "Jev": a SYSTEM-ONE model that answers TYPED questions about any state (text or JSON) in ~150 ms: noul (probability yes/no), choice (pick one named option, with probabilities), score (expected value on a rubric of levels). Many named questions can be asked in ONE request about the same state. Very cheap. It cannot see images.
- DeepInfra: vision-language models (Qwen3-VL, Gemma-3, Mistral-Small), large LLMs (Kimi-K2.6, Qwen3-235B, gpt-oss-120b, MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek), CLIP / text embeddings.
- MothQuantum: certified quantum random bytes (slow on real hardware, fast in simulator).
- Everything deterministic in the projector kernel is byte-exact integer C, so any device reproduces it.

The research vision: go beyond classic RL / neural nets / backprop. Learning as a HOLARCHY of first-person perspectives — cells -> tissues -> organs -> organisms -> families -> communities — with no central authority: a murmuration or kaleidoscope of many cheap viewpoints that see reality from different angles, help each other locally, and grow structure (guided growth) rather than being trained end-to-end. Typed system-one judgments are the "nerve impulses"; expensive models are rare "deliberations".

Propose 4 CONCRETE, NOVEL experiments that can be run THIS WEEK with exactly these tools on this projection problem (we have ground truth, so results are measurable). Each must use Jev in an essential, non-trivial way, name the level(s) of organization it lives at, and state a falsifiable hypothesis with the number that would confirm or refute it. Prefer ideas where many cheap local typed judgments replace one expensive global one, where structure grows, or where perspectives negotiate without a center.

Reply with JSON only:
{"ideas": [{"name": "<short>", "levels": ["cell"|"tissue"|"organ"|"organism"|"family"|"community"], "mechanism": "<3-5 sentences>", "jev_role": "<what Jev is asked, typed>", "hypothesis": "<falsifiable, with the measurement>", "cost": "<API calls estimate>", "beyond_classic_ml": "<one sentence: why this is not just RL/NN/backprop>"}]}
